key_insight: Layered compliant coatings reshape near-wall turbulent responses through surface stiffness, subsurface structure, thickness scaling, and damping.
engineering_relevance: The framework enables lower-cost screening of passive coating designs for potential skin-friction reduction before high-fidelity simulations or experiments.
method: Couple linearized fluid resolvent analysis with a through-thickness solid Galerkin model.
Represent layered viscoelastic coatings through a spectral surface-impedance operator.
Assess temporal stability and estimate drag changes using leading-order response covariances.
evidence_signal: At Reτ = 180, stiff panels approach rigid-wall behavior while more compliant panels modify near-wall low-rank responses; additional studies examine Reynolds-number scaling, damping, and layering.
watch_item: Drag changes are model-based estimates rather than demonstrated reductions, and unstable parameter regimes limit the relevance of steady harmonic responses.
paper_title: Resolvent-based modeling of turbulent flow over multilayer compliant surfaces
